title: Anhalt-Dessau agents in Prague → Prince Johann Georg I: Johann von Alairt's letters of 1610-11 in upside-down German, deciphered at the time except a slip of Nov 1611; the prince's cipher table and a slip key are unused
correspondents: Johann Loew; "Johann von Alairt"; Jacob Quelwitz → Johann Georg I of Anhalt-Dessau / Peter Meyer
shelfmark: Landesarchiv Sachsen-Anhalt, Z 44 (Abteilung Dessau) A 9a Ic Nr. 1 Bd. I-III, Nr. 2 Bd. I-IV, Nr. 3, Nr. 4 Bd. I, Nr. 5, Nr. 6 (all digitised)
folio_note: Images: https://recherche.landesarchiv.sachsen-anhalt.de/images//Z_44/A_9a_Ic_<volume>/max/Z_44__A_9a_Ic_<volume>__NNNN.jpg (e.g. Nr_2_Bd_I). Keys: Nr. 2 Bd. I image 6, 'Cifra ... Joannis Georgii Principis Anhalt', a sign alphabet a-z and a nomenclator 10-70; Nr. 2 Bd. II image 184, a slip with signs for 11 names and words (37 = Iudaeus, 68 = Einsidell). Alairt's letters from Prague with cipher, deciphered between the lines: Nr. 1 Bd. II images 152-153 (5 Apr 1610), 177 (19 Apr), 197 (4 May), 241-242 (18 May); Nr. 1 Bd. III images 41-42 (May), 154 (July), 263 (Aug). Undeciphered: Nr. 4 Bd. I image 400, an 8-line slip docketed 'praes. Dessau den 23. Novemb. 1611'.

links.label: Z 44 A 9a Ic Nr. 2 Bd. I

status: Checked image by image by Michael Brackx (issue #128, 27 Oct 2026); images 6, 241 and 400 confirmed here. The cipher in use is Alairt's: German in Latin script with every letter turned top to bottom (b/p, d/q, n/u, m/w trade places; e looks like o). Every cipher line of his 1610 letters has a decipherment in a second hand above it, except formulas. The Nov 1611 slip has none; its first line reads 'Will der Kayser bericht werden, dass der Hertz[og] von Braun[schweig] ...' (Brackx; agreed here). No letter in Nr. 1 Bd. I-III, Nr. 2 Bd. I-II, Nr. 3 or Nr. 4 Bd. I uses the prince's table or the slip key. Not searched: Nr. 2 Bd. III-IV (accounts), Nr. 5-6 (newsletters), Nr. 1 Bd. III image 80 (would not load). Christian I of Anhalt-Bernburg's cipher systems 1608-27 are in Z 18 A 9a Nr. 1/0. Target folder: targets/anhalt1610/ (in progress).
why: Intelligence from Rudolf II's Prague for the Calvinist Anhalt princes before the Union.
prior_art: open (checked 26 Oct 2026: known.py, quick web search).
known: 1610 letters deciphered at the time (interlinear); system identified as upside-down German by Michael Brackx.
open: The Nov 1611 slip; whether any letter uses the prince's table or the slip key.
